hints: Focus on what Tollens' reagent is really testing for, it only gives a silver mirror with an aldehyde, not with a ketone or an alcohol.
Remember hydrolysis replaces each C-Br with C-OH, so work out where the two OH groups end up for each dibromobutane.
If both OH groups land on the same carbon, apply the rule in the question to lose water and decide whether you get an aldehyde with CHO or a ketone with C=O in the middle.
walkthrough:
**Hydrolyse the dibromoalkane**

Complete hydrolysis replaces each Br with OH using aqueous NaOH and heat. Think of it simply as Br becomes OH.

$$\text{R-Br} + \text{OH}^- \rightarrow \text{R-OH} + \text{Br}^-$$

**Spot the unstable gem-diol**

If the two OH groups are on different carbons, the diol is stable. If both OH groups are on the same carbon, it is unstable and loses water.

$$\text{R-CH(OH)}_2 \rightarrow \text{R-CHO} + \text{H}_2\text{O}$$

**Link carbonyl type to Tollens'**

Loss of water from a C-1 gem-diol gives an aldehyde, $\text{R-CHO}$. Loss from a C-2 gem-diol gives a ketone, $\text{R-CO-R'}$. Only aldehydes reduce Tollens' reagent to silver metal.

$$\text{aldehyde} + \text{Tollens'} \rightarrow \text{silver mirror}$$

**Apply to 1,1-dibromobutane**

Hydrolysis of $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CHBr}_2$ gives $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH(OH)}_2$. This gem-diol on C-1 dehydrates to butanal.

$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH(OH)}_2 \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CHO} + \text{H}_2\text{O}$$

options.A: Hydrolysis gives the 1,1-diol, CH3CH2CH2CH(OH)2. Both OH are on C-1, so water is eliminated to give butanal, CH3CH2CH2CHO. Butanal is an aldehyde, so it gives a silver mirror with Tollens' reagent.
options.B: Hydrolysis gives CH3CH2CH(OH)CH2OH, a 1,2-diol. The OH groups are on different carbons, so no water is lost and no carbonyl is formed. With no aldehyde present, Tollens' test is negative.
options.C: Hydrolysis gives CH3CH(OH)CH2CH2OH, a 1,3-diol. The OH groups are on different carbons, so the diol is stable and no aldehyde or ketone is produced. Tollens' test is therefore negative.
options.D: Hydrolysis gives CH3CH2C(OH)2CH3, a 2,2-diol. It does lose water, but because the carbon is in the middle of the chain it forms butan-2-one, CH3CH2COCH3. This is a ketone, and ketones do not give a silver mirror with Tollens' reagent.
